posts.author: Tanarex
posts.body:
Dance of the Damned is an RPG with Puzzles and minigames.  It tests both mind and body. Using memory and reflexes, you must guide your adventurers past many perils. As your characters regain their skills, it will slowly unlock new features. This game has innuendos and a few suggestive comments. But otherwise pretty mild. I also have a Deviant Art page with backstory and past adventures with these humorous and incorrigible misfits.
Spoiler:
”Features”
[*]Hunters and Gatherers -  Collect various herbs, minerals, gems, meats, etc, from various sources.
[*]Once more with Feeling - Characters and townspeople now show emotions on their face graphics, which usually consist of eyes open, eyes closed, mouth open, and mouth closed. So...yay! Real emotions!
[*]Quest Journal - Now features a new quest log to keep track of objectives. Including Bonus Objectives and Secret Ones. What are the Secret ones? If I told you, it wouldn't be a secret.
[*]Crafting System - Create an assortment of potions, poisons, foods, beers, weapons, and much more. It's a simple crafting system.
[*]Trailblazers - Swim, Skate, Climb, and Move heavy obstacles with magical footwear.
[*]Achilles Heel - Discover the Strengths and Weaknesses of all 4 Characters.
[*]Sticky Fingers - Steal from enemies in Battle. There is also a chance to find something rare and one-of-a-kind items.
[*]Trophy Hunter -  By dealing the death blow with a specific skill, a party member can find unique materials.
[*]We are all Special Little Snowflakes - Each Character has their own set of skills and abilities.
[*]Does this hurt? Four different types of weapons cause unique types of damage. A new Weapon Master Book explains them.
[*]What's under the bed? - New Monster Catalogue added. Discover the enemy's strengths, weaknesses, and other useful info.
[*]Everything is Magic- A new magic book has been added to explain the magic system.
[*]You talk too much- At the beginning of a long dialogue, you will have three options. The long version: Full of humor, tasks, and world-building. The Short Version: Tells you what tasks you have to complete and nothing else. And just skip it, only recommended if you have seen the 1st or second one already. The quest giver will give you the short version if you forget.
Spoiler:
”Vincent's Jpurnal”
Date: Octenberg 25th.
"For weeks on end, our dreams were invaded, and the Curse of the Demore Mansion was upon us. The night terrors acted as both a summons and a warning. Enter the mansion or suffer madness and death, so like a moth to a flame, we were drawn. Each step we took seemed to leave a part of us behind. We begin to lose our identities, our skills, our abilities, and everything but our past, as if to taunt us so we can remember all that we have lost. The town of Demore had its own trials for us to help remind us of who we are. Although some of the tasks we were set upon were deadly, we were once again whole. Cannot a warrior recall how to fight without a battle? A thief to steal without a prize? A hunter to stalk without prey? We rose from the proving ground stronger than before, but would it be enough? We had just finished one gauntlet only to arrive at a far more dangerous one. The mansion itself loomed before us. We took one look back at the assembled townsfolk; they waved and shouted words of encouragement. Now that we know their secret, it was a cold comfort. They wondered if we would return victorious or become sacrifices for the
Dance of the Damned
."

” Tips, Advice, and Hidden Achievements”
Talk to Crazy Crofton every day. He may sound mad, but there is wisdom in his cryptic clues.
There is a limit to the amount of money in this game. So spend it wisely. There is no way to grind for experience or gold. No endless amounts of supplies to mine, harvest, or collect. No creatures drop gold.
The Innkeeper can help guide you if you get stuck.
There are secret achievements in each boss battle or leading up to it. There are other achievements throughout the game. A few offers one-of-a-kind rewards. Can you find them all and get the final achievement?
Death becomes you. Not only can you die in battle, but also on the world map and in certain multiple-choice options.
Open to suggestions and feedback.
If you see any resources that I have not accredited, let me know, and I will add them.

posts.author: Tanarex
posts.body:
Meeting Vincent
It had been a long day of checking animal traps and hunting small game when Vincent finally returned to his wood cabin. Only to discover voices coming from within. He lived alone and didn't usually have company. He pressed his ear against the door to see what surprises awaited him.
"We will wait till the watch and bounty hunters have moved on. I'm tired of running," the man said exhausted.
"Why you'd have to rob that merchant anyways?" a second man's voice asked.
"Because he was rich," The third voice replied.
"And now we have every mercenary, sell-sword and bounty hunter looking for us. Witha huge price on our heads." the second spoke angrily.
Vincent had heard enough from these uninvited guests. He casually walked right in.
"How much are you worth?" He asked them.
Startled they jumped and reach for their swords. "100 gold apiece," the first one said without thinking. Much to the annoyance of the other two.
"I mean, what's it matter to you?" he recovered.
"I could use 300 gold," Vincent spoke calmly. "I could use a new wood chopping ax." He raised his small wood hand ax to give them a good look. And a new crossbow." He glanced down to the worn crossbow swung from his side.
He could see from their attire they were outlaws. Robbing anyone who passed their territory of the road in the wilderness. They smelled like unbathed vagrants and were dirty.
"That's gonna be hard for you to collect. Since we outnumber you three to one. And we are all armed with swords." the third one had an unkempt beard and seemed to be the leader. Dressed in slightly better weather-worn traveling clothes.
"Now, if anyone comes looking for us, you'll tell them you haven't seen us. And we'll let you live."
Vincent didn't care for this plan. And he didn't want a log cabin that was built for one, to have three criminals stinking up the place.
"I have a better plan," he said simply. In his right hand he held a dead rabbit he retrieved from
one of his traps. "Catch!" he said suddenly to the dumbest of the outlaws.
Who dropped his sword to catch the dead rabbit he threw to him. With his hand free Vincent quickly and brutally punched him in the face. The outlaw
collapsed completely stunned and barely conscious.
"Idiot!" their leader yelled. "Why did you do that?!" he raged. "He said, "catch." The dumb one
mumbled before passing out.
"I've killed wolves and scared off bears. And you think you three intimidate me?' Vincent said fearlessly. "I should say two, now," he corrected himself.
The second outlaw raised his sword to strike. Vincent didn't move a muscle.
Instead, there was a loud clunk sound as the sword became embedded in the ceiling. These outlaws were unfamiliar with fighting in enclosed spaces. Still
holding ontop his embedded sword, Vincent stuck the second outlaw in the face too. He also fell to the floor like a sack of potatoes.
"Swordfights don't work well in small spaces," Vincent informed the final outlaw. He drew his crossbow at last. "Crossbows, however, do," He assured him.
It wasn't until later the next day while Vincent was chopping wood that he was hailed by the local watch. He sensed someone was watching him. Before
the watchmen and their captain came into the clearing.
"Hail, woodsman." The captain of the local watch called. "We are searching for three outlaws that robbed a merchant. He has offered up a bounty for
their capture."
"Then your search is over, "Vincent grinned.
He motioned for them to follow him to the side of the house. There they were shocked to find all three of the wanted men tied to trees. The three were untired and taken into custody.
"I believe there was a reward for their capture," Vincent reminded the watch
captain.
"Ah, yes," the watch captain soon overcame his disbelief. "Take this bounty slip and handed it into the Watchman's office for your reward." He handed
him a piece of paper.
"The bearer of this slip will receive payment to the capture or demise of The Callus Gang of 100 gold apiece alive. Or 50 gold apiece dead." the captain informed him.
"They didn't live up to their name," Vincent remarked.
"What?" the watch captain asked confused.
"They seemed pretty soft to me," Vincent said sly.
"Oh, the Callus Gang. Yes." The watch captain agreed.
"So you took down the entire gang by yourself?" the captain inquired.
He nodded.
"You might have the making of a bounty Hunter. Have you ever considered doing this for a living?" the captain asked.
"No. I just enjoy the simple life. Everything I need, I have right here," Vincent said serenely.
With a wave of his hand, he indicated his cabin.
"If you ever change your mind you can apply to the bounty hunter guild in Sendel," the Captain advised.
"We will be heading back now that these bandits have been caught. Next time you are in.."The Captain explained.
'I think I will go with you," Vincent interrupted.
"Ah...distrustful."The Captain said impressed. "Also a good trait for a bounty Hunter. Alright. The townsfolk will be interested to see the man
that single-handedly took down "The Callus Gang."
It wasn't until the rich fat merchant went to see the bandits that Vincent discovered something had gone wrong.
"Where is the fourth one? the merchant inquired.
Vincent immediately fled from the jail. With the bandit leader jeering him. "You are too late!" he mocked.
The fourth bandit was assigned as a lookout for the rest of The Callus gang. But fatigue and boredom soon took their toll on him. He had fallen asleep as the watchman strolled right pass the bushes he had concealed himself in. They had seen the rest of the gang tied up and had no reason to search for anyone else. He was awakened by their footsteps. He watched in silence as they were all carted away. He wanted revenge on the woodsman, but he had left with the others. All that was left to take it out on was a wood cabin.
Vincent saw the smoke from miles away. He had used some of his reward money to rent a horse. But even then it was already too late. His wood cabin was nothing but a smoldering ruin. The last thief had fled into the woods. Having extracted his pity retribution.
Hours later Vincent reappeared at the jail. He was dragging a badly beaten final member of the Callus Gang. Mercilessly he tossed him into a nearby cell.
"I'm gonna need to collect a bounty on this one too," He said to the watch's paymaster.
"What did you do to him?"The paymaster asked.
"He burns down my cabin. Then he insulted me by thinking he could hide in the woods," Vincent said bitterly. "Everything I had was in that cabin."
"Tell me where to find this Bounty Hunter Guild," He addressed the Watch Captain.
The End
Hope you enjoy this story filled with grammar errors and fragmented sentences. Let me know if you are interested in the other 3 characters. The game can be found here.
https://forums.rpgmakerweb.com/index.php?threads/dance-of-the-damned.74973/

It has been fixed. Still double-checking everything before uploading. 53:43 I removed all the fees for crafting so need to update the dialogue.  I had to reduce the MDF on the snake one since I accidentally made it unwinnable. I have since then fixed it. You won't be able to get to the Mansion. There are 10 Chapters planned in total. And I am still working on Chapter 7. Chapters 8, 9, and 10 don't exist yet.

posts.author: Zevia
posts.body:
I can leave additional written comments, if you'd like. Figured the video would better show my experience, though.
Any particular aspects you'd like me to focus on?

posts.author: Tanarex
posts.body: Well, there are already have 2 videos on YouTube with Let's Play people playing my game with commentary. Of course, both had game-breaking bugs that stopped their video short. Because I either forgot to update a face graphic I deleted or they talked to the Storehouse guard from the wrong side. All issues have been fixed. Anything you think is worth mentioning would be good. Characters, story, gameplay, humor, fun factor. I don't think anyone has passed my demo yet. It's about 2 hours long. Even the guys at ECCC only played it to the first boss fight before saying, "Thanks for letting me try your game." Then wandered off. But I guess when you are working with Unity and the Unreal Engine as they were RPG Maker games prolly seem lame.

posts.author: Zevia
posts.body:
Regarding your replies to the video:
Tanarex said:
31:09 You could have just selected optimize to equip the best gear.
Click to expand...
I never trust the optimize command in any game. What if a piece of gear lowers ATK, but raises MAT, and that's what I want? What if I don't? What if it lowers ATK by 2, but does elemental damage that's strong against what I'm going to be fighting soon? The optimize command would ignore that.
If I've played the game for awhile and seen the design and can be confident that the designer has only made gear that is straight numerical upgrades and doesn't allow for choice, then I may lean more on it, but that early on, I'd prefer to individually examine each piece.
Tanarex said:
35:14 Each character can only use a certain type of armor or weapon.
Click to expand...
As a new player, I don't know that, so I check. I don't know for sure that each character has unique sets of weapons and armor until I check for myself, unless the game tells me outright or there's some kind of readme file that came with the game that I took the time to read.
Otherwise, I might see, "Oh, this armor can be used by
two
people. Hmm, who could use the stats more?"
Tanarex said:
39:47 There was a blank page that was stopping the '!' from showing up on the Peddler. It has been fixed. Still double-checking everything before uploading.
Click to expand...
Those sorts of items are why I prefer doing video - I didn't even know there was anything wrong with the Peddler. Players don't know what they don't know, so I find video feedback to be much more useful in a lot of scenarios because, as the designer, you know exactly what you're looking for to "work" and what doesn't.
Additional thoughts in no particular order:
Spoiler
In the camp at the beginning, the balloon icons over each party member going around in a circle twice, then each waking up one at a time, are kind of awkward. It seems like all of them were supposed to be sleeping, then wake up at the same time, but "wait for complete" was checked for each character instead. It seems unintentional that they each go 1 by 1
Same feedback during the forest intro when they investigate the hidden camp - it's odd that only one character moves at a time and I think it would feel more natural if multiple people moved at once when it seemed appropriate
If the rats all approached at once and just let out a single text of "Squeak!" instead of one by one approaching and doing "squeak!", I think it would feel more like getting attacked by a swarm
I didn't notice when playing, but looking back over the video, the shadow effects from the campfire are impressive. The lighting on that map is really nice
The parallax mapping in general looks really good
For longer cutscenes of dialogue, I think it would help to have some additional blocking / movement. As an example, from 1:36 to 2:12, there are 14 show text commands with no pause in-between and the 4 of them just standing in a line staring forward. I like the way they bicker with each other, since it shows personality, like Firewind being an elf whose uses nature magic, but is a neat-freak that doesn't like to touch anything in nature, but with such static blocking, it kind of comes across flat. If the characters were facing each other when they talked, you could do something like have Firewind turn right and turn left when he's exasperated, giving him a bit of movement to highlight his attitude, or turn away when he scoffs. It would give the player a little more action to view along with the dialogue so it felt like they were watching a cutscene play out.
From 13:58 to 14:26 is another 14 messages with the same problem - good character-building dialogue between the party, but starts to get stale quickly due to how static it all is
I don't quite get the fork in the road during the intro - they look left and say "the port city of Tripor would be the fastest way" to their destination, but then they turn right and go that way. My first thought was that I must've misread the dialogue, but looking back over my video, I'm just as confused as when I was playing
The attacks play out
really
fast and I was having trouble trying to adjust my strategy as a result. For example, I wanted to see if Firewind's magic was more effective than his basic attack, or if certain spells were more effective than others, but it was so hard to catch the exact moment Firewind's ability went off and know for sure which damage / weakpoint / resist was his. I like that there are different abilities to play with and the descriptions are helpful in guiding me towards what their
intended
effectiveness is, but as a playtester and ultimately as a player, I like to try for myself and see what the actual outcome is. For how fast everything progresses, though, it's hard to adjust accordingly. I often felt like I was carefully choosing my abilities, selecting my targets, then watching a whirlwind of animations, numbers, and sound, and going, "... I couldn't actually follow what just happened there."
This may seem counterintuitive in conjunction with the previous bullet point, but I think the forest intro fight is too long. It doesn't seem like the intent is for it to be challenging, since it's entirely skippable and just supposed to be a story introduction, so reducing the health of the enemies to shorten the fight up quite a bit would probably be a good idea.
Especially given that explanations for what the abilities do are slowly introduced over the course of the rest of the game as everyone regains the abilities they lost when they get to town, it'd be fine if the battle was short enough that no matter what you chose, you were going to win, and the point was just to show their power level before it gets reduced upon arriving in town
I would've thought using the RTP music would make the game feel more generic, but I think you've made good choices with when to use it. It feels well-placed for setting what I assume is the intended mood
I do think the "gameover" music for the victory is a little odd, though. Even if I wasn't familiar with RPG Maker, it's a minor chord and kind of slow, so it feels like "downer" music that's a bit at odds for winning a fight
Does RPG Maker VX Ace make the shift key progress dialogue / act as a "confirm"? I had a few moments where I was holding shift to dash, but then dialogue would suddenly pop up and rapidly start skipping through pages until I quickly let go, but then had the problem of not knowing what I had just skipped. You can see examples at 13:57 or 55:54 where I kept getting confirm dialogues while I was trying to just run
If so, it might be good to look into just making dash on by default or adding some kind of toggle in the options to turn dash on or off by default. I'm pretty sure there are Plugins for such
There's a mistaken tile in the inn where the bear skin is hanging on the wall. You can see it at 32:01, the lower right, it's a grass / water tile
At some point during the development cycle, someone should do a proofread of all the text and correct spelling and grammar mistakes. The first couple I saw didn't stand out too much, but at some point it started to become a lot more noticeable and it impacts the overall perceived quality of the game
I was a bit confused at why, after the intro, I suddenly didn't have any of my skills. I know the characters eventually mention it in the inn, but it might be good to move that bit of dialogue to earlier, shortly after entering town
I like that just about everything appears to be capable of being examined, since it makes the world feel more populated and involved, plus it feels rewarding to explore when I'm given crafting resources. However, I picked up lots of stuff to use and was looking forward to unlocking the abilities that would use them, but then when I did, I was still short on a lot of items, so I didn't get to use the crafting. Maybe I needed to explore even more than I already had, but I think it would be good if the early crafting areas required fewer items or you were somehow given a kind of "starting cache" of materials so you could craft more things right away
I was really hesitant to use up any resources to craft or buy upgrades or stock up on items. I read the "tips for new players" before starting and it seems like there's quite a bit of warning against using anything because it's explicitly finite, so when I looked at weapon upgrades, I would usually think, "Well. Is 4 more ATK actually noticeable? Or will I want this money later?" Or crafting anything, I would think, "Well. Is this item going to be actually useful compared to what I
might
use the materials for later?" As a result, I didn't feel encouraged to engage with all the shops and systems in town, which is unfortunate, because they seem like, if I weren't so concerned about getting into an "unwinnable" state by just exploring and experimenting, they might be more fun to interact with
Particularly with the "HINTS" provided at the start of the game that suggests that buying things in the store is pretty much never a good idea and it's better to craft things than buy them, my takeaway was, "If you can't make it yet, don't buy it, just wait until you
can
make it", but then I didn't seem to have enough to ever make anything and I had a constant
As a general rule, I like crafting systems in games, but I think I'm overall not engaging with this one because the game and the hints seem to suggest I shouldn't play around with it unless I know what I'm doing
For example, at 1:00:25, I have 16 different crafting items already, but they're spread across so many professions that I couldn't actually make anything. It felt like what I
should
be doing is buying the supplies I was missing, but I didn't want to spend money because I didn't know if I would maybe come up with those supplies later - after all, the game told me I should craft instead of buy
The balloon icons highlighting what's useful to talk to is nice - if I get tired of exploring everything, I can just go straight to the icons for what I'm looking for, e.g. quests or tips
I like exploring the different shops and I think it's more realistic that you can't buy directly from them and, instead, they ship their products to the trading post - however, after awhile, I started to feel like there was no point in exploring the town as a result because nobody really had anything informative or interesting to say and I was never rewarded for interacting with anything in the shops beyond minor amounts of flavor. That could be an intentional design decision, though - only go to a shop once you're directed to it by a quest
I did like that exploring the town
other
than the shops rewarded me with crafting materials, as the game pushes you towards with crates and barrels and such
The quest system of having to learn each party member's strengths and then being quizzed on them is interesting
There's a bit of dialogue that's a little difficult to interpret and, at the time, seemed unnecessarily mean. When you finish the first quest, there's some text that says, "Congratulations! You have basic problem solving skills!" (at 40:16 in the video). It sounds sarcastic, like, "If you weren't able to solve this, I think you're stupid and lack even basic problem solving skills. And if you did solve it,
congrats, you're not a moron!
" It's difficult to tell tone through text, but maybe something like, "Congratulations! The party has earned basic problem solving skills!" would sound more like it was congratulating the player on unlocking the first set of passive skills for the party.
A deeper explanation of what the stats do might be nice. Jedd has lots of "raise the party's stats" abilities, but I have no idea what LUK does, so I'm not sure if I'm wasting a turn by having him use that ability or not

posts.author: Tanarex
posts.body:
The way I have armor and weapons set up is if more expensive than your previous armor/weapons then it has no negative stats. So you will always choose the best things you have. The only exception to this rule is the equipment that isn't armor or weapons since it ignores them by default.
Well, the first time you enter the weapon shop you see 4 upgraded versions of the character's default weapons. There are also shops that are special to each character that will unlock the only armor type they can use. Except for Brent. He uses the same shop as Firewind. I can add a note in their description on what type of weapon and armor they can use. I make the weapons and armor usable for one character each. The way the stats are set up grants a bonus to their skills, stats, and playstyles. Plus I didn't want Brent (The coward of the bunch) tanking for the group.
It says there were 4 character quests with '!' above their heads. One was outside. I saw you running around confused about what to do next in the INN. So my fault for that. I was still doing another playthrough to check everything. I am constantly 'improving' different things in my game. Because I am a perfectionist. You change one thing and it can mess up a whole bunch of other things.
I actually did that balloon thing on purpose. Some of them react faster than others to certain things.
I know. I just didn't know how to make multiple characters move at once. I'm not that great with computer stuff.
Well, they are only getting hit by half of the swarm. I feel like if the rats were swarming them they would all attack. But I get your point.
The shadow effects, lighting, and pretty much all the mapping in the game were done by Guiguimu. But I can be blamed for accidentally deleting a lot of it by messing with the game files.
I will try to make them more animated during dialogue.
Vincent was orientating himself on which direction to go.
Yeah, I think the messages during battle go by too fast too. But I have no idea it could be changed.
The intro fight isn't skippable if you choose 'skip intro'. It just takes you directly to the fight. Then plays out the remanded of the dialogue. Which I guess defeats the purpose of skipping the dialogue option.
I wanted the player to be able to try out the skills without worrying about killing the enemy too fast. Plus there is a hidden achievement that takes a while to complete. All the other characters would have to just defend and have nothing else to do while he completes it. One of the guys at the ECCC was playing it on my laptop and he was just using default attacks. Then the enemy started attacking and he said," Oh, damn." And he sat up and stopped goofing around. I said, "That's right. You have to pay attention."
Most of the music just had town 1, town 2, INN 1, INN 2. So it really was a no-brainer.
I think I just forgot I can change the game over music. I'll change it to something more upbeat.
13:58 Ahh.. yes that happened because it was in the middle of a parallel process. Yeah, it looks like shift also acts as a confirm. I never really thought about that. I have updated the controls message to reflect this.
I did have someone write a dash on/off snippet for me. Sometimes I want them to move quickly sometimes at normal speed, and sometimes slowly. I think the best option for this would be to make Shift has no other function than Dash. But I'm not sure how to fix that. On a side note, you can complete the Rabbit Habits mini-quest without using Dash. With about 3 seconds to spare.
32:01 Didn't notice that. Fixed.
I had my brother spell-check everything. But then I wrote more stuff and rewrote other stuff. I'm bad at speck-checking my stuff.
I guess it's the curse of the town. They don't realize it's gone till someone else brings it up. They are not doing anything that requires their combat skills. I can add something. But then it will make the conversation later redundant.
I have added one of every crafting item that can be found or won as a reward. But some of them are in the Government District. That can't be reached until after Chapter 5. I guess I could always have it open but I didn't want the players to get lost. There are certain mini-quests where you have to find something and don't want them checking the wrong district.
As for craftables, everything can be made for free if the shop is 'unlocked' and you have the mats.
If you don't feel like running from one shop to another you can just buy it for slightly more. You can also buy the raw materials for cheaper and craft them at the right shop. At first, it's only a few coins discount to DIY. In later Chapters, it starts to go up and you save more money on it. But it will also cost more to buy. You can also just buy all equipment and weapons for that Character's Chapter (The one who has to do the solo boss battle) without worrying about running out of money. The only downside is that you will have less money for one-use items. Like potions, food, drinks, poisons, etc. After the boss battle whatever extra money you have left over can be used to buy whatever you want. All the character quests reward money in the next chapter will easily cover any new weapons and equipment you might need for that character before a solo boss battle. You will find yourself in trouble if you spend it on the wrong character. It will tell you which character before the boss battle. Followed by an accept/reject option in case you need to gear up first.
You did find about half the hidden items. Seven of them are locked behind the Government District area. You know you have found them all when the achievement pops.
Many shops open up and allow you to craft/buy equipment/weapons/items from them. Some quests will require special items to advance the story that can only be made or bought at the shops. Also, many NPC will say something new each day. Adding a bit of lore, personality, and humor to the mix. A few NPCs have very important information to solve puzzles and clues.
You should also check behind buildings, trees, etc. Items can be hidden from view.
40:16 It was just some good-natured ribbing. There is a lot of sarcasm in my game. It wasn't meant to be mean-spirited. If you failed a character quest and a message popped up saying, "What are you an idiot?" Then that would be crossing the line.
The LUK stat is too complex to describe in the description. Adds a chance to add state aliments/debuff to enemies by a small percentage. While being able to resist debuffs/stats on the character.
Thank you for taking the time to review my game.
